passages.heading: Qualification indicators (promotion consideration)
passages.chapter: Chapter 3. Recommended Career Management Self-Development, by Rank
passages.body:
b. Most Qualified Indicators (SSG and SFC)
(1) Key Development Positions: 30-36 months of rated time at the appropriate level. (Applies to both SSG and SFC).
(2) Professional Military Education (PME): Distinguished Honor Graduate, Honor Graduate, or Commandant List. (Applies to both SSG and SFC).
(3) Civilian Education:
a. SSG: Working towards a completed associate's degree. Obtaining Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) sponsored certificates and other MOS- related certifications from the COOL website.
b. SFC: Completed associate's degree and working towards a bachelor's degree. Obtaining FAA sponsored certificates and other MOS-related certifications.
c. All Ranks: Distinguished Leader Award, Lean Six Sigma Black Belt.
(4) Physical Fitness: AFT score of 450 or above, with a score of 90 in each event, without event substitution. NCOs on permanent profile should strive to reach 80 points in participable events.
(5) Training: (Completing two or more courses, a pattern of consistently completing military training is recommended)
a. SSG: Battle Staff, Mission Command Digital Master Gunner Course, Equal Opportunity Leaders (EOL) Course, Sexual Harassment/Assault Response & Prevention (SHARP) Level I, Health and Holistic Fitness Integrator Course (H2F-I).
b. SFC: Army Knowledge Management Qualification Course, Battle Staff, Mission Command Digital Master Gunner Course.
(6) Assignments:
a. SSG: Drill Sergeant, CTC Observer/Coach Trainer, Special Mission Unit, Special Operations Aviation.
b. SFC: Senior Drill Sergeant, Small Group Leader, Aviation Proponent NCO, Talent Manager NCO, Special Mission Unit, Special Operations Aviation.
c. Other Broadening (All Ranks): Joint, NATO, Military Science Instructor, EOA/SARC, and AC/RC positions.
(7) Other Indicators: Expert Soldier Badge, Iron Sergeant, SGT Audie Murphy Club Inductee, SGT Morales Club Inductee, Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal (MOVSM), Army Best Squad of the Year, Drill Sergeant of the Year, NCO of the Year, Trainer of the Year (AAAA Functional Award), James H. McClellan Safety (AAAA National Award), Rodney J.T. Yano Non-Commissioned Officer of the Year (AAAA National Award), Gary G. Wetzel Army Aviation Soldier of the Year (AAAA National Award), Master Army Instructor Badge (MAIB), Army Gold Recruiter Badge, Professional Military Writing for peer reviewed articles (Published).
c. Highly Qualified Indicators (SSG and SFC)
(1) (1) Key Development Positions: 24-30 months of rated time at the appropriate level. (Applies to both SSG and SFC).
(2) Professional Military Education (PME): Recognition for achieving Superior Academic Achievement. (Applies to both SSG and SFC).
(3) Civilian Education:
a. SSG: Obtaining FAA sponsored certificates and other MOS-related certifications.
b. SFC: Working towards an associate's degree and obtaining FAA sponsored certificates.
c. All Ranks: Lean Six Sigma Green or Yellow Belt.
(1) Physical Fitness: AFT score of 400 or above, with a score of 80 in each event, without event substitution.
(2) Training: (Completing one or more courses, a pattern of consistently completing military training is recommended)
a. SSG: SERE-C, Ranger, Airborne, Air Assault.
b. SFC: SHARP Intermediate Course Graduate, Equal Opportunity Leader (EOL) Course, Health and Holistic Fitness Integrator Course (H2F-I). Airborne, Air Assault, SERE-C, Ranger.
(3) Assignments:
a. SSG: Recruiter, Small Group Leader, Instructor, Training Developer, Doctrine Developer
b. SFC: Recruiter, Training Developer, Doctrine Developer, Test and Evaluation NCO
c. Other Broadening (All Ranks): Joint, NATO, Military Science Instructor, EOA/SARC, and AC/RC positions.
(4) Other Indicators: Order of St. Michael, NCOA Individual Physical Fitness Award, Senior Army Instructor Badge (SAIB), Drill Sergeant Leader, NCO of the Quarter, Army Silver Recruiter Badge.
d. Most Qualified Indicators (1SG/MSG)
(1) Key Development Positions: 24+ months as a First Sergeant (most critical), Senior Aviation Operations Sergeant, or Air Traffic Control (ATC) Operations Chief.
(2) PME: Recognition as a Distinguished Honor Graduate, Honor Graduate, or Commandant’s List.
(3) Civilian Education: Completion of a bachelor's degree and working towards a higher-level degree.
(4) Physical Fitness: AFT score of 450 or above (90 in each event, no substitution).
(5) Training: (Completing four or more courses, a pattern of consistently completing military training is recommended) How the Army Runs, Capabilities Development, Manpower and Force Management, Army Knowledge Management, Battle Staff, Mission Command Digital Master Gunner, SHARP Intermediate, EOL, Health and Holistic Fitness Integrator Course (H2F-I), Airborne, Air Assault, SERE-C, Ranger.
(6) Assignments: Maximum of 36 months as an Equal Opportunity Advisor, Senior DARR NCO, Assistant Commandant, Proponent NCO, or Talent Management NCO. MSG/1SG within Special Mission Units will have completed 60 months within SMU and possess either SQI “C” or “T” with high enumerations not necessarily consecutive
e. Highly Qualified Indicators (1SG/MSG)
(1) Key Development Positions: 18-24 months as a First Sergeant, Senior Aviation Operations Sergeant, or ATC Operations Chief.
(2) PME: Recognition for achieving Superior Academic Achievement.
(3) Civilian Education: Completion of a bachelor's degree.
(4) Physical Fitness: AFT score of 400 or above (80 in each event, no substitution).
(5) Training: (Completing one to three courses, a pattern of consistently completing military training is recommended) From the list provided for "Most Qualified."
(6) Assignments: Maximum of 36 months in broadening roles with mid-level enumerations.
f. Most Qualified Indicators (15Z60 - SGM/CSM)
(1) Key Development Positions: 24+ months as a Command Sergeant Major or Operations Sergeant Major.
(2) PME: Recognition as a Distinguished Honor Graduate, Honor Graduate, or Commandant’s List.
(3) Civilian Education: Completion of a master's degree.
(4) Physical Fitness: AFT score of 450 or above (90 in each event, no substitution).
(5) Training: (Completing four or more courses, a pattern of consistently completing military training is recommended) From the list provided for "Most Qualified" MSG.
(6) Assignments: Maximum of 24 months in broadening assignments like Aviation Enlisted Assignment SGM, CSM CTC O/CT, Talent Manager, CCAD SGM, Commandant, OPFD SGM, SMU SGM, SOA SGM, etc
g. Highly Qualified Indicators (15Z60 - SGM/CSM)
(1) Key Development Positions: 18-24 months as a Command Sergeant Major or Operations Sergeant Major with mid-level enumerations.
(2) PME: Recognition for Superior Academic Achievement.
(3) Civilian Education: Completion of a bachelor's degree and working towards a higher-level degree.
(4) Physical Fitness: AFT score of 400 or above (80 in each event, no substitution).
(5) Training: (Completing one to three courses, a pattern of consistently completing military training is recommended) From the list provided for "Most Qualified" MSG.
(6) Assignments: Maximum of 24 months in broadening assignments like Aviation Enlisted Assignment SGM, CSM CTC O/CT, Talent Manager, CCAD SGM, Commandant, OPFD SGM, SMU SGM, SOA SGM, etc.

passages.heading: Private (PVT) E–1 to Specialist/Corporal (SPC/CPL) E-4 — recommended career management (applies to every MOS in this career management field)
passages.chapter: Chapter 3. Recommended Career Management Self-Development, by Rank
passages.body:
(1) Institutional Training: Advanced Individual Training.
(2) Military Study: Master AR 670–1; STP 21–1–SMCT; TM 1-1500-204-23; ATP 3- 04.1; ATP 3-04.7; ADP 6-22; TC 3-04.71; TC 4-02.1; TC 7-22.7, and all unit-level maintenance manuals.
(3) PME: Seize the first opportunity to attend Basic Leaders Course (BLC) upon promotion to Specialist/E4.

(6) Training: SERE-C, Airborne, Air Assault, Ranger.

passages.heading: Sergeant (SGT) E-5 — recommended career management (applies to every MOS in this career management field)
passages.chapter: Chapter 3. Recommended Career Management Self-Development, by Rank
passages.body:
(1) Institutional Training: Basic Leaders Course.
(2) Military Study: Master TC 7-22.7; ADP 6-22; STP 21–24–SMCT (Warrior Leader Skill Levels 2, 3, and 4); FM 6–22 Army Leadership, and all -10 level maintenance manuals.
(3) Development Focus: Self-motivated development becomes critical. Focus on broadening management and doctrinal knowledge (organizational behavior, personnel management, time management, Army OPS).
(4) PME: Strive for recognition as a Distinguished Honor Graduate, Honor Graduate, or on the Commandant’s List.
(5) Civilian Education: Enroll in a college degree program, pursuing credits towards an associate's degree, with the career goal of completing a bachelor's degree.
(6) Physical Fitness: Strive for an AFT score of 450 with a minimum score of 90 in each event.
(7) Training: SERE-C, Airborne, Air Assault, Ranger, Health and Holistic Fitness Integrator Course (H2F-I).

passages.chapter: Chapter 3. Recommended Career Management Self-Development, by Rank
passages.body:
(1) Institutional Training: Sergeants Major Academy.
(2) Military Study: Possess outstanding communication and public speaking skills.
(3) Development Focus: Study world politics, geo-political issues (DIMEFIL), and field manuals relating to Army OPS and current battle doctrine.

passages.heading: PVT-CPL — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 6. MOS 15B: Aircraft Powerplant Repairer
passages.body: Removes, replaces, services, prepares, preserves, cleans and stores engine assemblies or components. Disassembles, repairs, reassembles, adjusts, diagnostically test turbine engine systems, subsystems and components according to drawings, blueprints, directives, technical manuals. Assists in troubleshooting engines and rigging engine controls. Performs limited maintenance operational checks. Uses and performs operator maintenance on ground support equipment common and special tools. Maintains facilities for storage of flammable and hazardous materials. Requisitions and maintains shop and bench stock for repair of aircraft engines. Prepares requests for turn-ins and repair parts and engine components. Prepares forms and records related to MOS.

passages.heading: SGT — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 6. MOS 15B: Aircraft Powerplant Repairer
passages.body: Performs duties described in paragraph (1) and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel. Diagnoses and troubleshoots malfunctions in aircraft engines and their components. Participates in maintenance test flights as required. Monitors hazardous material control and storage.

passages.heading: SSG — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 6. MOS 15B: Aircraft Powerplant Repairer
passages.body: Supervises and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel performing duties described in paragraphs (1, 2) and evaluates the technical training program. Evaluates maintenance operations and facilities for compliance with directives, technical manuals, work standards, safety procedure and operational policies. Performs maintenance trend analysis and applies production control, quality control and other maintenance management principles, and procedures to aircraft engine maintenance and shop operations. Instructs personnel and conducts technical training in aircraft engine systems maintenance, supply and safety techniques. Monitors requisition of parts, tools, and supplies.

passages.heading: SFC — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 6. MOS 15B: Aircraft Powerplant Repairer
passages.body: At this point a 15B30 merges to become a 15K40. Critical

passages.heading: SFC — assignments
passages.chapter: Chapter 6. MOS 15B: Aircraft Powerplant Repairer
passages.body: assignments include Platoon Sergeant, Aircraft Production Control Supervisor, Aircraft Component Repairer Supervisor. See Chapter 12 for details.

passages.heading: MSG/1SG — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 6. MOS 15B: Aircraft Powerplant Repairer
passages.body: At this point, 15Ks merge into MOS 15Z, Aviation Senior Sergeant. See Chapter 23 for details.

passages.heading: PVT-CPL — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 7. MOS 15C: MQ-1 Operator
passages.body: Prepares and conducts air RSTA missions. Plans and analyzes flight missions. Deploys and redeploys the UAS ground and air system. Launches and recovers the air vehicle, performs pre-flight, in-flight and post-flight checks and procedures. Uses and performs operator maintenance and crew procedures performed on UAS air and ground equipment. Prepares forms and records related to UAS air and ground support equipment maintenance. Participates in the UAS site setup. Assists in maintaining facilities for storage of flammable and hazardous materials

passages.heading: SGT — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 7. MOS 15C: MQ-1 Operator
passages.body: Supervises and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel performing duties described in paragraphs (1, 2). Perform operational checks and scheduled inspections. Supervise site setup, participates in mission planning using maps, terrain studies, and intelligence reports. Participates in and supervise operator maintenance and crew procedures performed on UAS air and ground equipment. Conducts flight and academic instruction in accordance with the Aircrew Training Program (ATP). Monitor hazardous material control and storage.

passages.heading: SSG — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 7. MOS 15C: MQ-1 Operator
passages.body: Performs duties described in paragraph (1 and 2). Performs, supervises and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel performing UAS operations, maintenance and crew procedures. Performs site selection and supervises site setup of UAS ground equipment using maps, aerial photographs, terrain studies, and intelligence reports. Assist in intelligence collection and dissemination. Coordinate methods of employment to higher and adjacent units. Creates and maintains a mission and operational data base. Conducts flight and academic instruction in accordance with the Aircrew Training Program (ATP).

passages.heading: SFC — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 7. MOS 15C: MQ-1 Operator
passages.body: Performs duties shown in preceding skill levels and provides guidance to subordinate Soldiers. Supervise operations and activities of the platoon. Applies the military intelligence collection process and surveillance planning to UAS operations. Conducts flight and academic instruction in accordance with the Aircrew Training Program (ATP) for designated instructor positions.

passages.heading: MSG/1SG — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 7. MOS 15C: MQ-1 Operator
passages.body: At this point, 15Cs merge into MOS 15Z, Aviation Senior Sergeant. See Chapter for details.

passages.heading: PVT-CPL — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 8. MOS 15D: Aircraft Powertrain Repairer
passages.body: Removes and replaces powertrain quills, transmissions adapting parts, rotary wing hub and tanks. Disassembles friction dampers and hanger assemblies. Disassembles, repairs, reassembles, adjusts, balances and aligns powertrain components, systems and subsystems to include main and tail rotor hub assemblies according to drawings, blueprints, directives, technical manuals. Applies corrosion preventative procedures. Cleans, preserves and stores powertrain components. Performs nondestructive inspections on aircraft components and related items. Uses and performs operator maintenance on ground support equipment, common and special tools. Maintains facilities for storage of flammable and hazardous materials. Requisitions and maintains shop and bench stock for repair of aircraft powertrain systems and subsystems. Prepares request for turn-ins and repair parts for powertrain components. Prepares forms and records related to aircraft maintenance.

passages.heading: SGT — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 8. MOS 15D: Aircraft Powertrain Repairer
passages.body: Performs duties described in paragraph (1) and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel. Diagnoses and troubleshoots malfunctions in aircraft powertrain components and their subcomponents. Participates in maintenance test flights as required. Monitors hazardous material control and storage.

passages.heading: SSG — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 8. MOS 15D: Aircraft Powertrain Repairer
passages.body: Supervises and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel performing duties described in paragraphs (1, 2) and evaluates the technical training program. Evaluates maintenance operations and facilities for compliance with directives, technical manuals, work standards, safety procedures and operational policies. Performs maintenance trend analysis and applies production control, quality control and other maintenance management principles and procedures to aircraft powertrain system maintenance, nondestructive inspection and shop operations. Instructs personnel and conducts technical training in aircraft powertrain system maintenance, nondestructive inspection, supply and safety techniques. Monitors requisition of parts, tools, and supplies.

passages.heading: PVT-CPL — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 9. MOS 15F: Aircraft Electrician
passages.body: Diagnoses and troubleshoots malfunctions in electrical and electronic components, including solid state and transistorized subsystems. Repairs aircraft instrument systems. Applies principles of electricity/electronics, hydrostatic motion, pneumatics and hydraulics applicable to repair aircraft instrument systems. Removes, installs, repairs, adjusts and tests electrical/electronic elements of assemblies and components according to technical manuals, directives and safety procedures. Clean, preserve and store electrical/electronic components and aircraft instruments. Removes, repairs, services, installs, and troubleshoots nickel-cadmium batteries. Uses and performs operator maintenance on ground support equipment, common and special tools. Maintains facilities for storage of flammable and hazardous materials. Requisitions and maintains shop and bench stock for repair of aircraft electrical systems and subsystems. Prepares request for turn-ins and repair parts for electrical components. Prepares forms and records related to aircraft maintenance.

passages.heading: SGT — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 9. MOS 15F: Aircraft Electrician
passages.body: Performs duties described in paragraph (1) and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel. Diagnoses and troubleshoots malfunctions in aircraft electrical components and their subcomponents. Participate in maintenance test flights as required. Monitors hazardous material control and storage.

passages.heading: SSG — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 9. MOS 15F: Aircraft Electrician
passages.body: Supervises and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel performing duties described in paragraphs (1, 2) and evaluates the technical training program. Evaluate maintenance operations and facilities for compliance with directives, technical manuals, work standards, safety procedures and operational policies. Performs maintenance trend analysis and applies production control, quality control and other maintenance management principles and procedures to aircraft electrical system maintenance, nondestructive inspections and shop operations. Instructs personnel and conducts technical training in aircraft electrical systems maintenance, nondestructive inspections, supply and safety techniques. Monitors requisition of parts, tools, and supplies.

passages.heading: SFC — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 9. MOS 15F: Aircraft Electrician
passages.body: At this point a 15F30 merges to become a 15L40. Critical

passages.chapter: Chapter 9. MOS 15F: Aircraft Electrician
passages.body: At this point, 15Ls merge into MOS 15Z, Aviation Senior Sergeant. See Chapter 23 for details.

passages.heading: PVT-CPL — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 10. MOS 15G: Aircraft Structural Repairer
passages.body: Repairs and replaces aircraft structural components to include stingers, longerons, bulkheads, beams and aircraft skin according to drawings, blueprints, directives, technical manuals and safety procedures. Fabricate structural parts, forming blocks, and shapes metal using stretching, shrinking, and other metal forming techniques. Mixes and applies fiberglass materials. Makes emergency and permanent repairs to transparent plastic windows and enclosures. Uses common measuring tools, precision measuring gages, and alignment fixtures to perform structural repairs. Balances fixed-wing aircraft controls such as flags and ailerons. Mixes and applies primers and paints to aircraft surfaces. Apply corrosion control treatment to aircraft metals. Maintains facilities for storage of flammable and hazardous materials. Requisitions and maintains shop and bench stock for repair of aircraft structures. Prepares forms and records related to aircraft maintenance.

passages.heading: SGT — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 10. MOS 15G: Aircraft Structural Repairer
passages.body: Performs duties described in paragraph (1) and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel. Diagnoses airframe structural integrity IAW drawings, blueprints, directives, technical manuals and manufacturing engineers. Monitors hazardous material control and storage.

passages.heading: SSG — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 10. MOS 15G: Aircraft Structural Repairer
passages.body: Supervises and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel performing duties described in paragraphs (1, 2) and evaluates the technical training program. Evaluate maintenance operations and facilities for compliance with directives, technical manuals, work standards, safety procedures and operational policies. Performs maintenance trend analysis and applies production control, quality control and other maintenance management principles and procedures to aircraft electrical system maintenance, nondestructive inspections and shop operations. Instructs personnel and conducts technical training in aircraft structural repair, nondestructive inspections, supply and safety techniques. Monitors requisition of parts, tools, and supplies

passages.heading: SFC — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 10. MOS 15G: Aircraft Structural Repairer
passages.body: At this point a 15G30 merges to become a 15K40. Critical

passages.heading: PVT-CPL — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 11. MOS 15H: Aircraft Pneudraulics Repairer
passages.body: Removes, repairs, replaces, adjusts and tests pneudraulic systems, subsystems, assemblies, and components according to drawings, blueprints, directives, technical manuals, and safety procedures. Fabricates tubes and hoses. Diagnoses and troubleshoots malfunctions to pneudraulic systems and subsystems or components. Maintain facilities for storage of flammable and hazardous materials. Requisitions and maintains shop and bench stock for repair of aircraft structures. Prepares forms and records related to aircraft maintenance.

passages.heading: SGT — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 11. MOS 15H: Aircraft Pneudraulics Repairer
passages.body: Performs duties described in paragraph (1) and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel. Monitors hazardous material control and storage.

passages.heading: SSG — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 11. MOS 15H: Aircraft Pneudraulics Repairer
passages.body:

Performs maintenance trend analysis and applies production control, quality control and other maintenance management principles and procedures to aircraft pneudraulics maintenance, nondestructive inspections and shop operations. Instructs personnel and conducts technical training in aircraft pneudraulics repair, nondestructive inspections, supply and safety techniques. Monitors requisition of parts, tools, and supplies.

passages.heading: MSG/1SG — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 13. MOS 15L: Armament/Electrical/Avionics Repairer Supervisor
passages.body: At this point, 15Ls merge into MOS 15Z, Aviation Senior Sergeant. See Chapter 23 for details.

passages.heading: PVT-CPL — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 14. MOS 15M: MQ-1 Repairer
passages.body: Diagnoses, troubleshoots and repairs malfunctions in UAS electrical, avionics, radio frequency, propulsion, fuel, optical payload, and weapon systems components including solid state and transistorized subsystems according to pertinent technical manuals, directives and safety procedures. Remove and install unmanned aircraft system subassemblies. Performs inspections and periodic maintenance on the aircraft, ground control station, ground data terminal, takeoff and landing systems, and associated ground support equipment. Performs aircraft fueling and defueling operations. Serves as crewmember performing launch, operational and preventive checks and alignments on aircraft flight controls, stabilization systems, avionics and controlled cryptographic equipment. Troubleshoots equipment wiring harnesses, electrical components, and radio frequency paths using technical manuals and schematic drawings to diagnose, isolate faults, and effect repairs. Uses test sets and diagnostic equipment. Maintain records on all system equipment. Uses common and special tools. Maintains facilities for storage of flammable and hazardous materials. Prepares forms and records related to MOS.

passages.heading: SGT — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 14. MOS 15M: MQ-1 Repairer
passages.body: Performs duties described in paragraph (1) and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel. Serves as a crew chief for launch and recovery operations. Monitors hazardous material control and storage. Schedules maintenance on test, measurement and diagnostic equipment (TMDE). Alters or modifies material according to DA approved modification work orders.

passages.heading: SSG — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 14. MOS 15M: MQ-1 Repairer
passages.body: Supervises and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel performing duties described in paragraphs (1, 2) and evaluates the technical training program. Evaluates maintenance operations and facilities for compliance with directives, technical manuals, work standards, safety procedures and operational policies. Performs maintenance trend analysis and applies production control, quality control and other maintenance management principles and procedures. Computes basic weight and balance and ensures compliance with aircraft configuration control, Army Oil Analysis Program, and Test Measurement, and Diagnostic Equipment calibration. Performs technical inspections. Instructs personnel and conducts technical training in unmanned aircraft systems electrical, avionic, radio frequency, propulsion, fuel, optical payload, and weapon systems repair procedures and shop and flight line safety. Monitors requisition of parts, tools and supplies.

passages.heading: SFC — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 14. MOS 15M: MQ-1 Repairer
passages.body: Supervises unmanned aircraft systems maintenance and technical inspection activities. Determines man-hours, personnel, parts and facility requirements to repair unmanned aircraft systems and associated equipment. Plans maintenance areas, component repair, technical inspection techniques, and procedures, according to directives, technical manuals, work standards, and operational policies. Maintains supply economy and discipline. Supervise the unmanned aircraft systems technical training program. Prepares evaluations, special reports, and records pertaining to unmanned aircraft systems maintenance and related activities. Recommends and administers plans and policies.

passages.heading: MSG/1SG — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 14. MOS 15M: MQ-1 Repairer
passages.body: At this point, 15Ms merge into MOS 15Z, Aviation Senior Sergeant. See Chapter 23 for details.

passages.heading: PVT-CPL — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 15. MOS 15N: Avionic Mechanic
passages.body: Repairs, replaces, and performs operational and preventive checks and alignments on aircraft flight controls, stabilization systems, avionics and controlled cryptographic equipment. Troubleshoots equipment and traces avionic and cryptographic equipment wiring harnesses using technical manuals and schematic drawings to diagnose and isolate faults and effect repairs. Performs unit maintenance on special and common hand tools and test, measurement, and diagnostic equipment. Requisitions and maintains shop and bench stock for repair of aircraft avionics equipment. Maintains facilities for storage of flammable and hazardous materials. Prepares forms and records related to aircraft maintenance.

passages.heading: SGT — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 15. MOS 15N: Avionic Mechanic
passages.body: Performs duties described in paragraph (1) and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel. Schedules maintenance on test measurement and diagnostic equipment (TMDE). Alters or modifies material according to DA approved modification work orders. Monitors hazardous material control and storage.

passages.heading: SSG — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 15. MOS 15N: Avionic Mechanic
passages.body: Supervises and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel performing duties described in paragraphs (1, 2). Evaluates maintenance operations and facilities for compliance with directives, technical manuals, work standards, safety procedures and operational policies. Performs maintenance trend analysis and applies production control, quality control and other maintenance management principles and procedures to armament, electrical and avionics maintenance, nondestructive inspections, and shop operations. Instructs personnel and conducts technical training in avionic, COMSEC, flight control and stabilization equipment maintenance, repair, nondestructive inspections, supply, and safety techniques. Evaluates the technical training program. Monitors requisition of parts, tools, and supplies.

passages.chapter: Chapter 15. MOS 15N: Avionic Mechanic
passages.body: At this point a 15N30 merges to become a 15L40. Critical

passages.heading: MSG/1SG — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 15. MOS 15N: Avionic Mechanic
passages.body: At this point, 15Ls merge into MOS 15Z, Aviation Senior Sergeant. See Chapter 23 for details.

passages.heading: PVT-CPL — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 16. MOS 15P: Aviation Operations Specialist
passages.body: Processes cross-country and local flight clearances, including examination for conformance with flight rules and regulations. Prepares and maintains cross country kits. Checks accuracy of flight plans. Coordinates flight plans with all related agencies. Maintains flight information on inbound and outbound flights. Communicates with the proper agencies if flights are overdue. Alerts crash crew for emergencies. Maintains current file on aircraft flying regulations and navigation information such as Army, DoW and FAA regulations, DoW flight information publications (FLIPS) and aeronautical charts. Safeguards classified material. Knows terminology used in air navigation and is aware of air traffic control advisory radio procedures. Encodes, decodes and posts notices to airmen (NOTAMS). Interprets and posts weather reports. Maintain individual flight records and functional files. Maintain flight operations equipment in a tactical environment. Prepare, submit operator meaconing, intrusion, jamming and interference reports. Participates in maintaining situation map.

passages.heading: SGT — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 16. MOS 15P: Aviation Operations Specialist
passages.body: Supervises and instructs subordinates in proper work techniques and procedures. Reviews, consolidates and prepares technical reports. Knows procedures for reporting flight violations. Prepares situation map. Supervises receipt and transfer of classified material. Participates in the development of a tactical crash rescue system.

passages.heading: SSG — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 16. MOS 15P: Aviation Operations Specialist
passages.body: Supervises and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel performing duties described in paragraphs (1, 2). Supervises the preparation of the situation map. Assists in preparation of operations estimates and orders. Supervises airfield services and administration. Applies operational and administrative techniques in movement of military personnel and supplies by air. Perform administrative duties in aircraft accident investigations. Prepares operations letters.

passages.heading: SFC — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 16. MOS 15P: Aviation Operations Specialist
passages.body: Provides tactical and technical expertise to subordinates and superiors in aviation operations. Plans, coordinates and supervises activities pertaining to organization, training, combat operations and combat intelligence. Coordinates implementation of operations, training programs and communications activities. As an Aviation Operation Sergeant at Brigade Aviation Element (BAE) provide technical and doctrinal advice to the Chief of Operations (CHOPS). Receives and distributes relevant data from the Airspace Control Order (ACO) and Airspace Tasking Order (ATO). Ensures operation and maintenance requirements are met for section Air and Missile Defense Workstation (AMDWS), Forward Area Air Defense (FAAD), and Tactical Airspace Integration System (TAIS) equipment. As a platoon sergeant, coordinates the logistical, personnel and administrative support for all platoon elements.

passages.chapter: Chapter 16. MOS 15P: Aviation Operations Specialist

passages.heading: PVT-CPL — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 17. MOS 15Q: Air Traffic Control Operator
passages.body: Operates fixed and tactical ATC towers, Ground Control Approach GCA radars and airspace information centers (AICs). Operates and maintains vehicles, tactical/fixed base ATC equipment and navigational aids (NAVAIDs). Assist in the installation and relocation of tactical ATC facilities. Applies air traffic control rules, procedures and regulations. Processes flight plan data. Formulates and issues ATC clearances, advisories and control information. Maintains logs, records, files and recordings of voice communications. Interprets and relays Notices to Airmen (NOTAM) information. Reads and interprets DoW Flight Information Publications (FLIPS) and aeronautical charts. Analyzes air traffic to identify and resolve potential conflicts. Controls airborne and ground traffic on and in the vicinity of the airport. Updates Automated Terminal Information Service (ATIS) and performs radarscope alignments. Coordinates terminal/enroute control. Provides approach control services, conducts precision radar instrument approaches, provide (AIC) services and control tower services. As a qualified member of a tactical air control team (TACT), establishes and controls landing zones (LZs), helicopter landing zones (HLZs), drop zones (DZs) and pick-up zones (PZs).

passages.heading: SGT — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 17. MOS 15Q: Air Traffic Control Operator

Supervises a shift in a tactical or fixed tower, radar, or AIC. Services as a tactical air control team (TACT) leader in a tactical terminal control system (TTCS), deploys team as advance party to remote areas to secure and set up forward area refueling and rearming points (FARPS), LZs, HLZs, DZs and PZs. Maintains current DoW and DOT/FAA publications, ATC facility logs, forms, records and situation maps. Prepares, briefs and disseminates Aviator’s Procedures Guide (APG) to supported aviation units. Assist in the preparation of TERPS

passages.heading: SSG — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 17. MOS 15Q: Air Traffic Control Operator
passages.body: Supervises and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel performing duties described in paragraphs (1, 2). Serves as facility chief at low-density towers, radar or airspace information centers. Serve as facility chief in tactical towers, GCA radars and AICs. Administer ATC facility. Formulates and coordinates letters of agreement, operations letters and facility memorandums. Prepares duty rosters and assigns duties to personnel. Ensures facility flight check requirements are met for navigational aids, radar and radio communications equipment. Plans and organizes ATC activities for tower, GCA radar, airspace information centers and verifies facility compliance with Army and FAA standards. Evaluates ATC operations and work performance. Reviews and prepares reports. Coordinate ATC activities with other facilities. Prepares and updates situation maps. Assists in the preparation of Standard Instrument Approach/Enroute/Departure Procedures (TERPS) for assigned facility/NAVAID.

passages.heading: SFC — overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 17. MOS 15Q: Air Traffic Control Operator
passages.body: Serves as facility chief in high density and designated remotely located fixed base towers, GCA radar, or AICs. Plans, organizes and supervises ATC facilities. Establishes and supervises the facility training and rating program. Advises in the preparation of TERPS. Ensure proper utilization and coordination of maintenance support. Prepares and interprets orders and reports. As an A2C2 liaison at division and echelons above corps (EAC) assists in the development and execution of the Airspace Control Order (ACO) and Airspace Tasking Order (ATO). Coordinates, deconflicts and integrates all airspace control measures for division, corps, or EAC commanders. As a platoon sergeant, coordinates the logistical, personnel and administrative support for all platoon elements and deploys platoon to remote locations in support of forward aviation assets. Prepares and coordinates TERPS data with the appropriate FAA Department of the Army regional representative. Conduct briefings for senior commanders on the current tactical airspace situation. An NCO should have 24-36 months of rated facility chief or Platoon Sergeant time to be competitive with their peers.

passages.body: Merges into MOS 15Z. NCOs are tracked with PDSI B4B for specific ATC SGM positions (e.g., USAASA, ATC Senior SGT).

passages.heading: PVT-CPL — overview

Troubleshoots and repairs electrical components, flight controllers, and radio frequency systems using diagnostic tools. passages.heading: MSG/1SG (15Z50) — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 23. MOS 15Z: Aviation Senior Sergeant
passages.body: The MSG serves as a versatile senior leader who operates either as the Operations NCOIC in the Battalion Operations (S3) section or as a Production Control NCOIC. When positioned as the Battalion Operations NCOIC, the MSG oversees the flight operations section, compiles complex technical reports, facilitates Battalion level training and readiness meetings, and enforces flight violation reporting protocols. When assigned as the Production Control NCOIC, the MSG exercises supervision over aviation unit, intermediate, and depot maintenance activities, effectively managing a diverse mix of aircraft maintenance and component repair MOSs. In this logistical role, the MSG communicates detailed technical timelines on a regular or as needed basis regarding Operational Readiness (OR) rate, Fully Mission Capable (FMC), and Non-Mission Capable (NMC) aircraft to respective owning units. By blending tactical operations with synchronized logistical control, the MSG ensures that all assigned aircraft are strictly maintained to airworthiness standards and kept in a state of mission readiness.

passages.heading: MSG/1SG (15Z50) — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 23. MOS 15Z: Aviation Senior Sergeant
passages.body: The 1SG serves as Senior Enlisted Advisor to the Company Commander for a multi-functional aviation company, providing operational and administrative oversight across flight operations, specialized maintenance, air traffic control, and unmanned systems. Directs the health, welfare, morale, professional development, and tactical readiness of all assigned personnel. Manages critical Soldier programs including promotions, awards, physical fitness, and Army Body Composition Program compliance while enforcing military discipline, safety protocols, and HAZMAT regulations. Monitors the Fighter Management and Aircrew Training Programs to ensure Non-Rated Crewmembers and UAS Operators maintain currency and readiness levels. Coordinates with airfield management and Air Traffic Control to safely integrate crewed and unmanned assets into tactical airspace. Partners with Production and Quality Control to synchronize phase maintenance, maximizing Operational Readiness and Fully Mission Capable ratings across Powerplant, Powertrain, Pneudraulics, Avionics, Structural, and Ground Control Station shops. Drives Command Supply Discipline to ensure parts availability and oversees the secure handling, transport, and loading of munitions. The key developmental position for MOS 15Z50 is First Sergeant in an Aviation Company.

passages.heading: SGM/CSM (15Z60) — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 23. MOS 15Z: Aviation Senior Sergeant
passages.body: The SGM serves as the NCOIC within the Brigade Operations (S3) section, synchronizing the activities of the staff and planning complex multi-domain training for the commander. Operating as the operational backbone of the headquarters, the SGM integrates staff officers and noncommissioned officers into the Military Decision-Making Process (MDMP) and coordinates high-level staff functions to ensure mission orders are executed effectively. By combining comprehensive training management with battlefield command post leadership, the SGM mentors and develops senior NCOs across the battalion and brigade to enforce the highest standards of professional conduct, discipline, and operational readiness.

passages.heading: SGM/CSM (15Z60) — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 23. MOS 15Z: Aviation Senior Sergeant
passages.body:
The CSM serves as the Senior Enlisted Advisor to the commander within a Combat Aviation Brigade (CAB), providing strategic, tactical, and technical guidance to the staff on all aviation operations. As the principal enlisted advisor, the CSM is directly involved with all matters affecting the command, with a primary focus on ensuring Soldier welfare, morale, and training readiness. In this capacity, the CSM oversees multiple vital readiness initiatives, including the Aviation Maintenance Training Program (AMTP), unit physical fitness, and the Army Body Composition Program (ABCP). Monitors the Fighter Management and Aircrew Training Programs to ensure Non- Rated Crewmembers and UAS Operators maintain currency and readiness levels. By blending high-level operational oversight with disciplined mentorship, the CSM enforces the highest standards of professional conduct, military appearance, and combat readiness throughout the CAB.
b. Goals for Development:
(1) MSG/1SG: The critical assignment for a 15Z50 is successful completion of time as a First Sergeant. Accumulating 24+ months in a coded 15Z50 position is critical for future promotion and progression.
(2) SGM/CSM: The pinnacle achievement for a 15Z60 is selection and successful service as a Battalion or Brigade Command Sergeant Major, leading large-scale multi-domain operations and enterprise-level logistics.
